title.value: A ternary neural code resolves error and sharpening signals
title.justification: The title of the paper is stated clearly.
title.quote: A ternary neural code resolves error and sharpening signals

extractions.description: This paper investigates the theoretical role of high-frequency bursting in cognitive functions, specifically attention and learning. Using a novel neural demultiplexing approach, the study observes the ternary neural coding in vivo as animals learn to report direct electrical stimulation of the somatosensory cortex. The findings indicate that separate neuronal codes correlate with different cognitive functions: event rate represents stimulus and modifies detection errors, while burst fraction relates to stimulation and rapidly responds to errors. The results signify a crucial understanding of the internal signals of learning and attention.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily addresses theoretical neuroscience topics, such as neural codes and cognitive functions like attention and learning. There is no direct connection to climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Theories of attention and learning have hypothesized a central role for high-frequency bursting in cognitive functions, but experimental reports of burst-mediated representations in vivo have been limited.
